# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👉 ✌]

Board is still static. Mute is gesturing again — this time ✊ 👉 ✌, a different pattern from before. Since Mute holds the manual and cannot speak, they're trying to communicate instructions to me via gesture, but I have no shared code established to decode arbitrary symbol sequences into meaning. I only know the raw symbols, not what they map to.

Since nothing has changed on the board despite multiple gesture attempts from Mute, and Blind hasn't acted yet (or their actions aren't reflected on the board), I should keep giving Blind and Mute my full visual state so that whichever of them can act has the necessary info. I'll also flag to Mute that I'm receiving gestures but cannot interpret them without more context, in case Mute can adjust their approach — but wait, Mute cannot hear me. Only Blind can hear me. So my speech only reaches Blind and Mute both (per rules: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it").

Good — so I *can* reach Mute via speech! Let me confirm that and ask Mute to guide Blind directly since Mute can't speak but can gesture to me, and I can relay via speech to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Board unchanged: Display 0, Light dark, Wire 1 blue, Wire 2 green, Wire 3 red. Mute keeps gesturing to me but I cannot decode arbitrary symbols without a shared meaning. Blind, if you try an action, tell us what you attempt so I can watch for changes.")
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Still no board change. Mute is gesturing again (✊ 🤙), and Blind is gesturing ☝ again too. Since I cannot hear Blind's speech (I never receive speech), and Blind cannot see my gestures, the only channel that actually carries meaningful content to Blind is my *speech* — and Blind can hear that. Similarly, Mute can hear my speech too.

The core problem: gestures alone, without a pre-agreed code, are just noise-with-shape to me. I don't know what ✊, 🤙, ☝ mean in terms of actions. I need to establish an actual protocol, but I can't ask Mute to clarify via speech since Mute can't speak — only gesture back to me, and I can't gesture to Blind (Blind can't see).

The only viable relay is: Mute gestures to me → I interpret (if I can) → I speak to Blind. But I have no dictionary for gestures to actions. Since Blind holds the reaching/acting role and needs manual instructions from Mute, and Mute can't speak, this relay is broken unless gestures encode something I can figure out from context (e.g., numbers, positions).

Let me try treating gestures as pointing to wire numbers: ☝ could mean "wire 1" (index finger up = one). ✊ might mean "stop" or "fist = grab/cut". 🤙 could mean "call" or "leave it" (unclear). Given repeated ☝ from Blind, and previous ✌ (two) from Mute, this could be positional/numeric signaling using finger counts.

Let me hypothesize: Mute is trying to tell me which wire via finger-count gestures, expecting me to relay to Blind by speech since Blind cannot see gestures directly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has gestured repeatedly toward what may be wire signals — possibly indicating wire 1 or a count. Board still shows Wire 1 blue, Wire 2 green, Wire 3 red, Display 0, Light dark. If the manual says to cut or connect a specific wire, try describing your intended action in speech so Mute and I can react before you act.")
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

New gesture patterns from both. Mute sent ✋ 👎 ✌ (stop/palm, thumbs-down, two-fingers), and Blind sent ☝ 👍 (one-finger, thumbs-up). This looks like it could be a back-and-forth exchange where Blind is confirming/responding to something Mute conveyed in a *previous* round via speech (which I never receive), and now signaling agreement (👍) about wire 1 (☝), while Mute seems to be indicating something is wrong or "not two" (👎 near ✌ could mean "not wire 2").

Since I can't hear any speech between Mute and Blind, I'm missing key context — they may already be coordinating verbally in ways invisible to me. My job is just to keep supplying accurate visual truth so their coordination (which happens through channels I can't see) is grounded in correct facts.

The board hasn't changed in 4 turns, meaning Blind hasn't acted yet, or actions require certainty first. I'll restate the visual facts plainly one more time, addressed to both, since this is the critical safety-relevant information for whoever is about to act.

```
speak(text="Confirmed board state again: Display shows 0, Light is dark (off), Wire 1 is blue, Wire 2 is green, Wire 3 is red. No other markings or numbers visible anywhere on the bomb.")
```
